item.title: Preprimary education laws and women’s empowerment later in life
item.content:encoded:
Nature Human Behaviour, Published online: 04 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41562-026-02608-z

Across nearly 6.7 million women in 117 low- and middle-income countries, eligibility under national preprimary education laws was associated with higher educational enrolment and completion, more gender-egalitarian attitudes, more favourable empowerment-related behaviours and greater reproductive autonomy.
item.dc:title: Preprimary education laws and women’s empowerment later in life

item.title: Preprimary education laws and women’s gender attitudes, empowerment and reproductive autonomy in 117 low- and middle-income countries
item.content:encoded:
Nature Human Behaviour, Published online: 04 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41562-026-02583-5

Lou et al. find that eligibility for preprimary education is linked to more gender-equitable attitudes, greater empowerment and reproductive autonomy, and lower levels of adolescent marriage and childbearing across low- and middle-income countries.
item.dc:title: Preprimary education laws and women’s gender attitudes, empowerment and reproductive autonomy in 117 low- and middle-income countries
